questions.text: School Financial Management: Prevent embezzlement: (1) Digital fee collection (mobile money vs cash); (2) Audited financial statements; (3) Procurement transparency (textbooks, construction); (4) Budget oversight (Board of Management); (5) Asset register maintenance; (6) Debt management; (7) Donor fund reporting.
questions.evidence_required: Audit reports, Mobile money statements, Procurement minutes, Asset register
questions.africa_specific_notes: Cash fees often stolen. Procurement fraud (ghost supplies) common. Digital payments increase transparency.

questions.text: EdTech Business Model Sustainability: Viability of provider: (1) Unit economics (CAC vs LTV); (2) Path to profitability (vs grant dependence); (3) Pricing sustainability (affordable but covers costs?); (4) Burn rate; (5) Investor backing; (6) Revenue diversification (B2B vs B2C); (7) Market saturation risk.
questions.evidence_required: Financial model, Investor updates, Unit economics analysis
questions.africa_specific_notes: Many EdTechs rely on grants/donors. When funding dries up, they vanish, leaving schools stranded.

questions.text: Anti-Plagiarism & Cheating Culture: Promote honesty: (1) Plagiarism detection tools usage; (2) Honor code enforcement; (3) Exam supervision quality; (4) Consequences for cheating; (5) 'Contract cheating' prevention (essay mills); (6) Faculty integrity (not selling grades); (7) Student awareness training.
questions.evidence_required: Plagiarism reports, Disciplinary records, Honor code
questions.africa_specific_notes: Cheating normalized in some contexts due to high stakes. 'Essay mills' target students. Faculty integrity key.

questions.text: Ethical Research Practices: For higher ed: (1) IRB/Ethics committee approval; (2) Data fabrication prevention; (3) Predatory journal avoidance; (4) Student contribution recognition; (5) Conflict of interest disclosure; (6) Research funding transparency; (7) Local relevance of research.
questions.evidence_required: IRB minutes, Publication list, Ethics policy
questions.africa_specific_notes: Pressure to publish leads to predatory journals. 'Helicopter research' (Westerners taking data) is an issue.

questions.text: Truth in Advertising (Education): Honest marketing: (1) Job placement claims verification; (2) 'International' status claims; (3) Facility representation (photos vs reality); (4) Hidden fee disclosure in ads; (5) Success story representativeness; (6) Partner logo usage rights; (7) Accreditation status clarity.
questions.evidence_required: Marketing materials, Placement data verification, Facility photos
questions.africa_specific_notes: Schools often promise 'international jobs' or 'partnerships' that don't exist. Misleading ads exploit aspirations.

questions.text: Predatory Lending & Scholarships: Fair financial aid: (1) Student loan terms transparency (interest rates); (2) Scholarship criteria fairness; (3) 'Free' laptop schemes (hidden costs?); (4) Income Share Agreement (ISA) terms; (5) Debt collection ethics; (6) Financial literacy training for borrowers; (7) Default consequences.
questions.evidence_required: Loan contracts, Scholarship selection minutes, ISA terms
questions.africa_specific_notes: Predatory loans for school fees common. ISAs emerging but need regulation. Students often sign without understanding debt.

questions.text: Gender Equity in Education: Support for girls: (1) Female enrollment/retention rates; (2) STEM participation for girls; (3) Menstrual hygiene support (sanitary pads/toilets); (4) Re-entry policy for teen mothers; (5) Gender-responsive pedagogy; (6) Female teacher role models; (7) GBV prevention.
questions.evidence_required: Enrollment data by gender, Sanitation audit, Re-entry policy docs
questions.africa_specific_notes: Girls drop out due to lack of pads, pregnancy, or early marriage. Schools must actively support retention.

questions.text: Disability Inclusion: Access for special needs: (1) Physical accessibility (ramps, toilets); (2) Assistive technology availability; (3) Specialized teacher training; (4) Curriculum adaptation (Braille, Sign Language); (5) Anti-stigma programs; (6) Assessment accommodation (extra time); (7) Individualized Education Plans (IEPs).
questions.evidence_required: Accessibility audit, Assistive tech inventory, IEP samples
questions.africa_specific_notes: Disabled children often hidden or excluded. 'Inclusive education' often just means placement without support.

scoring_notes: Layer 5 (Integrity) for Education in SSA: Financial integrity prevents resource theft. Academic integrity protects the value of degrees. Inclusion (Gender/Disability) is a moral and development imperative.
